paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus' teaching comes from God, and you find that out by wanting to do God's will, not by collecting diplomas. The crowd asked how He got such learning without studying, and Jesus said, "My teaching is not My own… It comes from Him who sent Me." (John 7:15-16) Then He said, "If anyone desires to do His will, he will know whether My teaching is from God or whether I speak on My own." (John 7:17) So the door isn't a big brain, it's a willing heart, and I wish somebody had told me that before I spent years thinking a dusty drawer made me unqualified for anything!

Notice what else Jesus said. "Stop judging by outward appearances, and start judging justly." (John 7:24) The people of Jerusalem did exactly the opposite: they figured they knew where He was from, so they figured they knew who He was. (John 7:27) Jesus told them, "You know Me, and you know where I am from," but they did not know the One who sent Him. (John 7:28) We do this too, friend, when we size up something in two seconds and call it settled, and then we're SHOCKED when it turns out to be bigger than our first look.

So what do you do with that today? Come to God's Word ready to obey it, not just ready to grade it. Ask Him to help you see past the surface, to what He is actually saying. And this story isn't over, because the crowd is still wondering what Jesus means, and the questions are only getting bigger.
